summary: Some animals may never be brought on the mizbe'ach, and if even one gets mixed with others, all of them become forbidden. The mishnah lists them, like an animal set aside for avodah zarah or one that was worshipped.

chunks.en: All animals that are forbidden on the mizbe'ach
chunks.st: With regard to all animals whose sacrifice on the altar is prohibited, if they are intermingled with animals whose sacrifice is permitted,

chunks.en: make a mixture forbidden, no matter how few they are:
chunks.st: they prohibit the entire mixture of animals in any amount, regardless of the ratio of permitted to prohibited animals.
chunks.stMore: These are the animals whose sacrifice is prohibited:

chunks.en: an animal used for a terrible sin, in two ways,
chunks.st: An animal that copulated with a person, and an animal that was the object of bestiality,

words.note: An animal used for a very bad, forbidden act.

chunks.en: one set aside for avodah zarah, one that was worshipped,
chunks.st: and the set-aside, and one that was worshipped, and an animal that was given as

chunks.en: a forbidden payment, and the price of a dog,
chunks.st: payment to a prostitute or as the price of a dog, or an animal crossbred from a mixture of

words.note: An animal given as payment for a forbidden act.
An animal given in exchange for a dog.

chunks.en: an animal mixed from two kinds, a treifah,
chunks.st: diverse kinds, or an animal with a wound that will cause it to die within twelve months [tereifa], or an animal

words.note: An animal whose parents are two different kinds.
An animal with an injury that will make it die within a year.

chunks.en: and one born from the side.
chunks.st: born by caesarean section.

words.note: Born through a cut in its mother, not in the normal way.

chunks.en: Which is the "set aside" one?
chunks.st: Which is the animal that is set-aside?

chunks.en: One set aside for avodah zarah.
chunks.st: It is an animal that is set aside for idol worship.

chunks.en: It itself is forbidden,
chunks.st: The animal itself is prohibited,

chunks.en: but what is on it is allowed.
chunks.st: but that which is upon it, e.g., its jewelry and garments, is permitted to be sold in order to purchase an animal to be sacrificed.

chunks.en: Which is the "worshipped" one?
chunks.st: And which is the animal that was worshipped?

chunks.en: Any animal that people worship.
chunks.st: It is any animal that a person worships as an object of idol worship.

chunks.en: It and what is on it are forbidden.
chunks.st: In this case, the sacrifice of both the animal itself and an animal purchased using the money from the sale of that which is upon it is prohibited.

chunks.en: But both of these may be eaten.
chunks.st: And the consumption of both this, the animal designated for idol worship, and that, the animal worshipped, is permitted.

summary: An animal given as payment for a forbidden act may not be brought as a korban. The mishnah explains which payment counts, and Rebbi and the Sages argue about one case.

chunks.en: What is a forbidden payment?
chunks.st: And which is the case of an animal used as payment to a prostitute, which is prohibited as a sacrifice?

chunks.en: If someone says to a woman who sins,
chunks.st: It is the case of one who says to a prostitute:

words.note: A woman who sins in a forbidden way.

chunks.en: "Here is this lamb as your pay,"
chunks.st: Here is this lamb as your fee.

chunks.en: even if there were a hundred,
chunks.st: Even if they were one hundred lambs that he gave her,

chunks.en: all of them are forbidden.
chunks.st: all of them are considered as payment to a prostitute and are prohibited.

chunks.en: And also if someone says to his friend,
chunks.st: And likewise, in the case of one who says to another:

chunks.en: "Here is this lamb
chunks.st: Here is this lamb and in return

chunks.en: for a forbidden thing between your maidservant and my servant,"
chunks.st: your maidservant will lie with my slave and engage in intercourse with him,

chunks.en: Rebbi says:
chunks.st: Rabbi Meir says:

chunks.en: It is not a forbidden payment.
chunks.st: Its halakhic status is not that of payment to a prostitute,

chunks.en: And the Sages say: It is a forbidden payment.
chunks.st: and the Rabbis say: Its halakhic status is that of payment to a prostitute.

summary: An animal given in exchange for a dog may not be brought as a korban, even when partners divide their animals. The Torah forbids only these two cases, and the babies of these animals are allowed.

chunks.en: What is the price of a dog?
chunks.st: And which is the case where an animal has the halakhic status of the price of a dog, and it is therefore prohibited to sacrifice the animal on the altar?

chunks.en: If someone says to his friend,
chunks.st: It is the case of one who says to another:

chunks.en: "Here is this lamb
chunks.st: Here is this lamb

chunks.en: in place of this dog."
chunks.st: in place of a dog.

chunks.en: And also two partners who divided their animals:
chunks.st: And likewise, this prohibition applies in the case of two partners who divided their common property, which included nineteen lambs and one dog, and

chunks.en: one took ten lambs,
chunks.st: one took ten lambs

chunks.en: and the other took nine and a dog.
chunks.st: and the other one took nine lambs and a dog.

chunks.en: The ones taken in place of the dog
chunks.st: Sacrifice of the ten lambs taken by the partner in exchange for the nine lambs and the dog

chunks.en: are forbidden; the ones with the dog are allowed.
chunks.st: is prohibited, and sacrifice of the nine lambs that were taken by the partner with the dog

chunks.en: But a dog's payment and the price of a zonah
chunks.st: is permitted. With regard to lambs given as payment to another for engaging in intercourse with his dog, or as the price of a prostitute to purchase her as his maidservant,

chunks.en: are allowed,
chunks.st: their sacrifice is permitted,

chunks.en: as it says,
chunks.st: as it is stated: “As both of them are an abomination to the Lord your God” (Deuteronomy 23:19),

chunks.en: "both of them": two, and not four.
chunks.st: from which it is inferred: Two are prohibited, payment to a prostitute and the price of a dog, and not four, i.e., the additional two cases of payment for intercourse with a dog and the price of a prostitute, which are permitted.

chunks.en: Their babies are allowed,
chunks.st: Furthermore, with regard to the two prohibited cases of payment to a prostitute and the price of a dog, sacrifice of their offspring is permitted,

chunks.en: as it says "them,"
chunks.st: as it is stated “them,”

chunks.en: and not their babies.
chunks.st: and not their offspring.

summary: If the forbidden payment was money, it may be used to buy a korban, but wine, oil and flour are forbidden. Holy things given are still allowed, but birds become forbidden, as the Torah says "for any vow."

chunks.en: If he gave her money,
chunks.st: If one gave money to a prostitute as her payment,

chunks.en: it is allowed.
chunks.st: it is permitted to purchase an offering with that money, as the money itself is not sacrificed.

chunks.en: Wine, oil,
chunks.st: If he paid her with wine, or oil,

chunks.en: flour, and anything like these
chunks.st: or flour, or any other item the like of

chunks.en: that is brought on the mizbe'ach,
chunks.st: which is sacrificed on the altar, sacrifice of those items

chunks.en: is forbidden. If he gave her holy things,
chunks.st: is prohibited. If he gave her consecrated items for her services,

chunks.en: they are allowed.
chunks.st: their sacrifice is permitted.
chunks.stMore: Since they were already consecrated, they do not belong to him, and one cannot prohibit an item that is not his.

chunks.en: Birds are forbidden.
chunks.st: If he paid her with non-sacred birds, their sacrifice is prohibited. The mishna elaborates:

chunks.en: We might have thought:
chunks.st: As, by right, it should be inferred a fortiori:

chunks.en: If holy animals,
chunks.st: If in the case of consecrated items,

chunks.en: which a blemish makes unfit,
chunks.st: which a blemish disqualifies,

chunks.en: do not become a forbidden payment or price,
chunks.st: the prohibition of payment to a prostitute and the price of a dog do not take effect with regard to them;

chunks.en: then birds, which a blemish does not make unfit,
chunks.st: with regard to a bird, which a blemish does not disqualify,

chunks.en: shouldn't it make sense that
chunks.st: is it not right that the prohibition of

chunks.en: payment and price should not take hold on them?
chunks.st: payment to a prostitute and the price of a dog should not take effect with regard to them?

chunks.en: So the Torah says:
chunks.st: Therefore, the verse states: “

chunks.en: "For any vow,"
chunks.st: You shall not bring the payment of a prostitute, or the price of a dog, into the House of the Lord your God for any vow” (Deuteronomy 23:19).

chunks.en: to include birds.
chunks.st: This serves to include the bird in the prohibition.

summary: The babies of animals that are forbidden on the mizbe'ach are allowed. The Sages argue about the baby of a treifah, and holy animals that became treifah cannot be redeemed, because we do not redeem holy animals to feed them to dogs.

chunks.en: All animals forbidden on the mizbe'ach,
chunks.st: With regard to all animals whose sacrifice on the altar is prohibited,

chunks.en: their babies are allowed.
chunks.st: sacrifice of their offspring is permitted.

chunks.en: The baby of a treifah: Rabbi Eliezer says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer says: The offspring of an animal with a wound that will cause it to die within twelve months [tereifa]

chunks.en: It may not be brought on the mizbe'ach.
chunks.st: shall not be sacrificed on the altar.

chunks.en: And the Sages say:
chunks.st: But the Rabbis say:

chunks.he: יִקְרָב. רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶן אַנְטִיגְנוֹס אוֹמֵר,
chunks.en: It may be brought. Rabbi Chanina ben Antigonus says:
chunks.st: It shall be sacrificed. Rabbi Ḥanina ben Antigonus says:

chunks.en: A healthy animal that nursed from a treifah
chunks.st: A kosher animal that suckled from a tereifa

chunks.en: may not be brought on the mizbe'ach.
chunks.st: is disqualified from sacrifice on the altar.

chunks.en: All holy animals that became treifah
chunks.st: With regard to all sacrificial animals that became tereifot,

chunks.en: may not be redeemed,
chunks.st: one may not redeem them and render them non-sacred,

chunks.he: שֶׁאֵין פּוֹדִים אֶת הַקֳּדָשִׁים לְהַאֲכִילָן לִכְלָבִים:
chunks.en: because we do not redeem holy animals to feed them to dogs.
chunks.st: as their consumption is forbidden and one does not redeem sacrificial animals to feed them to dogs, as this is considered a degradation of sacrificial animals.
